questions.skill: Predict how changing a parameter changes the situation
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel rider's height is h(t) = 12 + 10sin(πt/15) m after t seconds. The wheel is replaced by one of the same size that turns twice as fast. In the new model h(t) = 12 + 10sin(Bt), what is B? Give B exactly, in terms of π.
questions.prompt_markup: A Ferris wheel rider's height is h(t) = 12 + 10sin(πt/15) m after t seconds. The wheel is replaced by one of the same size that turns twice as fast. In the new model h(t) = 12 + 10sin(Bt), what is B? Give B exactly, in terms of π.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the exact value. Twice as fast halves the period from 30 s to 15 s, so B = 2π/15.

questions.prompt: How can the frequency be read from the graph of a periodic function?
questions.prompt_markup: How can the frequency be read from the graph of a periodic function?

choices.text: Read the maximum height of the graph, which is the number of cycles per unit of the input.
Find the length of one cycle (the period) and take its reciprocal, the number of cycles per unit of the input.
Find half the difference between the maximum and the minimum, which is the number of cycles per unit.
Count the number of times the graph crosses the x-axis in the window shown; that count is the frequency.

questions.correct_answer: Find the length of one cycle (the period) and take its reciprocal, the number of cycles per unit of the input.
questions.grading_note: Frequency = 1/period. The others give the maximum, a count that depends on the midline, or the amplitude.
